3. Respondent No.2 entered appearance by filing affidavit in opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition. The case of respondent No.2 in short, is that, the status of the petitioner is different from that of the status of the normal citizens of the country. The report of the Special Branch of Police dated 25-10-2015, reveals that there are as many as 14 criminal cases pandering against the petitioner. The petitioner is fugitive from justice in Jessore Kotwali Police Station Case No. 15 dated 5-10-2015 under sections 15(3)/25D of the Special Powers Act, 1974 read with sections 4/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908. Under Rule 6(1)(2) of the Bangladesh Passport Order, 1973, respondent No. 2 enjoys discretionary power to grant or to refuse passport to any person. According to Rule 5(2) of the aforesaid Order, 1973, respondent No. 2 referred the matter to the Special Branch, Bangladesh Police for enquiry. The Special Branch after enquiry submitted report on 11-10- 2015. Since the petitioner is fugitive from justice he is not entitled to a passport. Respondent No.2 rightly refused to the petitioner. In fact, the petitioner being a fugitive from justice cannot claim to have to a passport. Therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

 4. The petitioner, however, filed .a supplementary affidavit against the affidavit in opposition filed by respondent No.2. In the supplementary affidavit the petitioner stated that on 7-12- 2015, he was granted bail by the High Court Division in Jessore Kotwali Police Station Case No. 15 dated 5-10-2015. In fact, the petitioner was never a fugitive from justice. 

 6. Mr Md Mokleshur Rahman, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of opposite party No.2, on the other hand, submits that the petitioner is fugitive from justice and that there are as many as 14 criminal cases pending against him. He further submits that under section 6( 1 )(2) of the Bangladesh Passport Order, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as the Order, 1973), the authority enjoys the discretion to grant or refuse passport to any person. He lastly submits that as per the report of the Special Branch, the petitioner is not entitled to a passport. 

 8. It appears from the record that the petitioner had a passport being No. is A-0158834. According to the decision of the Government, the old passports have been obsolete and all the citizens of the country have been requested to collect a Machine Readable Passport Annexure-B to the writ petition reveals that respondent No. 2 gave "delivery slip" to the petitioner stating that the passport would be delivered to the petitioner on 13-10-2015. From the order dated 7th December, 2015 (Annexure-C to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner) passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 48298 of 2015, we find that the accused-petitioner was granted bail by the High Court Division, in Jessore-Kotwali Police Station Case No. 15 dated 5-10-2015. Therefore, the allegation against the petitioner that he is a fugitive from justice does no stand good. There is no denial of fact that under section 6( 1 )(2) of the Order, 1973 the authority enjoys the powers to grant or refuse passport to any person.  23. Reverting back to the case in hand, the petitioner had a passport and during this time he has not earned any disqualification as per section 6(1 )(2) of the Order, 1973 to get a new passport.
